browser_artifact.note: Built with cargo build --release --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p anny-wasm, then wasm-bindgen --target web, from the final merge-gate tree. A rebuild from the same tree reproduces this digest byte for byte (verified with cmp), so the qualified artifact is this source revision. Size alone does not identify it: the previous revision produced a different digest at a similar size, because panic locations embed file and line. This revision also carries the caller-input validation in the GPU entry points, which is most of the growth over the previous 2,321,153 bytes. Both browser suites were re-run against the digest recorded here.

c_abi_smoke: ABI 1: 13718 vertices, 27420 faces; pose sessions match evaluate exactly (f64+f32) and survive anny_model_free. The final-review correction that declared the borrowed session ahead of its Arc owner was hammered by a throwaway harness (not committed): 200 pose updates on a session whose model handle had already been freed and bit-identical to the reference, 200 f64 and 200 f32 create/update/free cycles, and 60 sessions destroyed after their model, all clean under MALLOC_CHECK_=3 and MALLOC_PERTURB_=170. Swapping the field order back still passed the same harness on this host, so the fix is an invariant fix rather than an observable-crash fix: the session's Drop never dereferences the borrowed model

unity_players.note: Both players build from the same scene and generate the same character through the native plugin - the rebuilt 3,863,512-byte libanny.so (sha256 37f5c50c...) staged from this tree, whose copies inside both built players were verified to be that same file, so neither player can be running the pre-review binary. Geometry, topology, influence width and signed volume are identical across backends; the signed volume differs only in the last float digit. Each run also measures the per-update cost in the player and checks that AnnyCharacter.Evaluations advanced by exactly two per measured iteration. The phenotype figure moved from 0.57 ms (Mono) and 0.70 ms (IL2CPP) because the player's character runs in AnnyUpdateMode.Skinned and a full shape update now rebuilds the phenotype-dependent bind geometry, bind poses and rig - the correction that stops Unity skinning the old body's rest surface. Pose-only updates, which are the per-frame path, are unchanged at roughly 0.3 ms. The numbers were re-measured on an idle machine because the build-time run was contended; the shape-change cost is the honest price of the corrected behaviour, not a regression in the evaluation itself.
